group_assessment.weighting: A narrative literature review (searched to January 2024, four databases, four keywords, no stated screening or appraisal procedure) of two monoamine-transport disorders, DTDS and PKDYS2. Reference-signature content is useful; the review is internally inconsistent in at least one place (anticholinergic and benzodiazepine use in DTDS). It contains no WWOX content.

entries.proposition: The review's method is a keyword search of four databases to January 2024 with no stated appraisal.
entries.snippet: This literature review included many published studies until January 2024.

entries.proposition: DTDS gives elevated CSF HVA with normal 5-HIAA; the stated discriminating ratio is HVA to 5-HIAA above 4.
entries.snippet: Therefore, another useful finding is an HVA to 5-HIAA ratio > 4 [8,9,11].

entries.proposition: PKDYS2 (VMAT2) is described as having normal CSF HVA and 5-HIAA, so a CSF panel can be normal in a monoamine storage disorder.
entries.snippet: Individuals with this condition have normal CSF neurotransmitters, with HVA and 5-HIAA levels within normal limits [12].

entries.proposition: CSF HVA and 5-HIAA are affected by drugs, and sampling and handling must follow strict protocols.
entries.snippet: It must be noted that the levels of HVA and 5-HIAA can be affected by several different groups of drugs [15].

entries.proposition: EEG is described as normal in both disorders.
entries.snippet: Electroencephalography (EEG) and electromyography and nerve conduction studies (ENMG) have always been found to be normal in both DTDS and PKDYS2 [16,18,19].

entries.proposition: Oculogyric crisis and dystonia are sometimes misdiagnosed as epilepsy.
entries.snippet: Sometimes, patients with oculogyric crises and dystonia are misdiagnosed with epilepsy [13].

entries.proposition: Brain MRI in PKDYS2 may show a dorsal brainstem T2 signal with restricted diffusion, in one cited report.
entries.snippet: brain MRI with abnormally high T2 signal intensity with restricted diffusion in the dorsal brainstem can be noted [13]

entries.proposition: Internal inconsistency: the text says DTDS patients are not treated with anticholinergics and benzodiazepines, while Table 2 lists anticholinergic and GABAergic agents against DTDS.
entries.snippet: In contrast, patients with DTDS are not treated with anticholinergics and benzodiazepines.

entries.proposition: Table 2 lists anticholinergic medications for generalized and segmental dystonia in DTDS.
entries.snippet: Anticholinergic medications | Generalized and segmental dystonia | Dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome

entries.proposition: Dopaminergic drugs can worsen hypotonia and cause hyperkinesia at higher doses in PKDYS2 case reports.
entries.snippet: This improved dystonic posture, but when the dose was increased to 0.01 mg/kg/day, it worsened hypotonia, irritability, and sleep difficulties.
